R1.rule: When measuring or reasoning about +mos-a16 codegen cost, never assume the ambient mode is 8-bit (M=1).

R4.rule: When measuring +mos-a16 codegen, empirically check whether a given rep/sep is attributable to the op under study or to the surrounding mode.

R5.rule: When evaluating a codegen change, always build the real code shape and diff the bytes before deciding it is a win.

R6.rule: After measuring, gate the native 16-bit form so it fires only where it wins.

R7.rule: Ship a gated, no-regression modest win even if the gain is small.

R8.rule: When telling the user to fill in a free-form field or make an open choice, state the single recommended value as the instruction rather than listing options.

R9.rule: Do not tell the user that a free-form field is arbitrary (e.g., "use anything" or "call it whatever") when giving the recommended value for it.

R10.rule: When choosing a recommended value for a free-form field, pick the best value and follow existing naming conventions in the project.

R11.rule: Give the recommended value flatly as the step instruction, without hedging.

R12.rule: If a value genuinely must vary, still lead with the recommended value.

R13.rule: Apply the recommended-value-as-instruction approach to on-screen instructions printed by scripts, not only to chat replies.

R14.rule: Lead with the recommended option and do not front the weaker option when presenting choices.

R15.rule: When a checkpoint is reached, commit the work as a checkpoint and do not mention push or remote sync state.

R16.rule: Push only when the user explicitly asks, and when asked, report only that the push is done.

R17.rule: Do not repeat the commit/push standard operating procedure in every response.

R18.rule: Do not state that changes are not pushed or note that the user did not ask for a push.

R19.rule: Do not report how many commits origin/main is behind the local branch.

R20.rule: Do not end responses with offers to push or fast-forward push changes.

R22.rule: Keep turn summaries focused on the actual work, such as what changed and verification results, rather than git-state narration.

R23.rule: When the user has stated a clear end goal, do not keep pausing to ask which sub-path to take.

R24.rule: When the user has stated a clear end goal, pick a path, execute through to the deliverable, and then report.

R28.rule: When finishing one phase of a multi-phase goal, keep going to the next phase without handing control back.
